Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family holiday is approaching, which is a traditional time for everyone to reconnect.
Expectation2: Ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards
Situation2: A routine audit is scheduled far ahead, leaving ample time to update documentation
Story:
I sat at my desk, the hum of the computer blending with the distant laughter of my grandchildren in the living room. The calendar notification blinked: “Family holiday next week.” My daughter had called earlier, reminding me how much the kids looked forward to our annual tradition—board games, stories, and late-night talks. I knew how important it was to be present, to keep those connections strong, especially as the years slipped by.

But as I opened my email, another reminder popped up: the upcoming safety audit at work. It was still weeks away, but the new regulations were complex, and the documentation needed a thorough overhaul. My team depended on me to set the standard, to catch the small errors before they became big problems. The expectation was clear—no shortcuts, no missed details.

I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in. My family needed me to be there, fully present, not distracted by work. My colleagues needed me to lead, to ensure everything was perfect. I stared at the screen, heart tugged in two directions, wondering how I could possibly meet everyone’s expectations.
